title: The Clockmaker and the New Railway

paragraphs.en: The museum's clockmaker began his tour at dawn, asking visitors why a town had once needed several different times. Before the advent of the railway, a local clock could follow sunrise and reach noon slightly earlier than a clock in the next valley. Medieval travelers rarely noticed the difference. A punctual train, however, required simultaneous agreement across distance. The outset of the exhibition showed how a gradual technical change became an epoch in public life: people learned to obey schedules set beyond the boundaries of their own community.
paragraphs.zh: 博物馆钟表师在黎明开始导览，问访客一座城镇过去为何需要几种不同时间。铁路出现之前，本地钟表可能依据日出计时，比邻谷钟表稍早抵达正午。中世纪旅人很少注意差别，但准点列车需要不同地方同时达成一致。展览开头展示渐进技术变化如何成为公共生活中的新纪元：人们学会遵从在自身社区之外制定的时刻表。

paragraphs.en: An apprentice's diary described the transition. At twelve, he had begun work in a repair shop; at thirteen, he could read a complicated dial; at fourteen, he maintained the tower mechanism. On his birthday at fifteen, he received a new calendar of railway duties. At sixteen, he worked overtime before a public anniversary, and at seventeen he trained another assistant. By eighteen, the need to keep accurate records was obvious. At nineteen, he had learned that haste could damage a delicate instrument more quickly than ignorance. Growing skill involved judgment, not simply spending more years beside a bench.
paragraphs.zh: 学徒日记描述了这种转变。十二岁时他开始在修理店工作，十三岁能看懂复杂表盘，十四岁维护塔钟机械。十五岁生日时，他收到铁路工作的新版日程。十六岁时，他在公共周年庆前加班；十七岁开始培训助手。十八岁时，准确记录的必要性已很明确。十九岁时，他懂得匆忙比无知更容易损坏精密仪器。技艺增长涉及判断，而不只是多在工作台旁待几年。

paragraphs.en: The diary also challenged the fantasy of perpetual work. One entry described eleven missed meals during a difficult repair, another forty hours of labor in a fortnight. The apprentice had hitherto believed every deadline must be met at any cost. His mentor argued that an intermittent fault needed patient observation, because its duration could not be predicted from one test. A subsequent page recorded a revised plan: zero unnecessary adjustments, regular breaks, and enough daylight to examine wear. In the meantime, a replacement clock would serve the station till the original mechanism became reliable again.
paragraphs.zh: 日记也挑战了永不停歇工作的幻想。一篇记下困难维修中错过十一顿饭，另一篇记下两周内劳动四十小时。学徒此前相信任何期限都必须不计代价满足。导师认为间歇性故障需要耐心观察，因为一次测试无法预测持续时间。后来的页面记录修改方案：不作无必要调整、定期休息、利用充足日光检查磨损。与此同时，车站先用替代钟表，直到原机械重新可靠。

paragraphs.en: A later section followed the town through the autumn of industrial expansion. Seventy arrivals became eighty, then ninety each weekday, and workers feared that precious minutes might elapse while passengers missed a connection. On the eve of a new timetable, the clockmaker checked the signals tonight rather than leaving everything for the morning. He returned sometime after midnight and inspected the result afterward. Lately, he noted, neighbors spoke as though standard time had existed forever. Yet it had not appeared overnight. Its apparent permanence depended on repeated maintenance, training, and cooperation among people whose work usually remained unseen.
paragraphs.zh: 后面的展区追溯工业扩张之秋的城镇。每个工作日的到站次数由七十增至八十、再到九十，工人担心耽误会导致错过转车。新时刻表实施前夕，钟表师决定今晚检查信号，而不是把一切留到早晨。他在午夜后的某个时候返回，随后检验结果。他记下，最近邻居说话仿佛标准时间永远存在。但它不是一夜之间出现的，其看似永恒的稳定依赖持续维护、培训，以及通常不被看见的劳动者之间的合作。

paragraphs.en: At the tour's end, visitors compared the railway clock with their own phones. Modern devices could coordinate meetings instantly, but they still relied on institutions and technical decisions. The clockmaker rejected the claim that greater precision was an eternal guarantee of better life. Accurate time could prevent accidents, yet schedules could also become instruments of unreasonable pressure. What mattered was how a community used its accuracy. A well-maintained clock served people best when they retained enough freedom to question the demands made in its name, rather than treating every measurable delay as a moral failure.
paragraphs.zh: 导览结束时，访客把铁路钟表与自己的手机比较。现代设备能即时协调会议，但仍依赖机构和技术决定。钟表师不赞同“更高精度永远保证更好生活”的说法。准确时间能够预防事故，但时刻表也可能成为施加不合理压力的工具。关键是共同体如何运用准确性。维护良好的钟表最好能够服务人，同时给人足够自由，质疑以准时之名提出的要求，而不是把每次可测量的迟延都视为道德失败。
